scope: Backup-service lifecycle and protected native repository recovery; synthetic application-agnostic data on one disposable Hetzner K3s cluster.

source.binding: Each run recorded working-tree SHA256 before execution. All implementation/chart inputs, its executed runner and artifacts helper were compared with Git blobs in testedContentCommit and matched; other runners were not inputs to that run. No image was published.

environment.restic: restic 0.19.1 compiled with go1.26.4 on linux/amd64
environment.storage: Independent primary and secondary local-path PVCs, with separate native repository identities and passwords.

scenarios.name: Native startup
scenarios.details: Both declared repositories initialized with no configured source; a configured source with confirmed empty native history initialized a secondary. Existing primary identity survived stop/start with unavailable recovery credentials and hostname.

scenarios.name: Exclusive ownership and queued work
scenarios.details: A second application could not admit the owned PVC. An older queued copy refused the changed generation before native destination access.

scenarios.name: Primary installation and storage replacement
scenarios.details: Old Helm release, endpoint, PVC, credentials and original client were deleted. A new installation reconstructed both retained points using the surviving secondary and independently supplied configuration/credentials, with no manual initialization or release step.

scenarios.name: Recovery and access after replacement
scenarios.details: Older point restored with matching SHA256; newer marker retained. Reader writes and incorrect credentials were denied, while a valid writer created a new native backup.

scenarios.name: Interrupted reconstruction
scenarios.details: Deleting the executing worker Pod with a 30-second graceful period interrupted native copy. Failure remained across controller restart; secondary locks were released without unlock. A fresh target reconstructed successfully.

scenarios.name: Durable stop during recovery
scenarios.details: Stop withdrew service and cancelled native recovery. The target retained its transition marker, local/secondary locks were released, controller restart remained stopped and later run intent did not clear failure.

scenarios.name: Durable stop during replication
scenarios.details: Stop cancelled a real running copy, suspended new work, and survived controller restart without new copy Jobs. Stopped acknowledged Deployment/ReplicaSet scale-down and no active PVC users; secondary locks were released without unlock.

scenarios.name: Independent secondary availability
scenarios.details: Byte-correct older-point restores succeeded from the secondary while interrupted-recovery, stop-recovery and replication scenarios had active native copy work.

scenarios.name: Damaged local and recovery state
scenarios.details: Nonempty incomplete local state was refused without initializing it. A corrupt secondary snapshot that native snapshots --json omitted with exit zero was detected by strict list/cat inventory, leaving the empty target uninitialized.

scenarios.name: Unreachable recovery
scenarios.details: DNS failure exhausted Restic native backend retries and became Failed. No target config was initialized; no custom retry or shortened native timeout was introduced.

scenarios.name: Endpoint regression
scenarios.details: HTTPS role/repository isolation, path normalization, reader lock access, append-only writer protection, native lock exclusion, selected maintenance and intact-PVC Deployment replacement.

scenarios.name: Scheduled replication regression
scenarios.details: Real CronJob scheduling, destination-authentication failure isolated from primary publication, catch-up, idempotence, native maintenance lock conflicts with exit 11, independent secondary history after primary deletion and cache-disabled direct restore.

limitations: One-cluster installation/storage replacement, not an actual cross-provider outage or independent provider fencing qualification. Replacement requires confirmed source stop/retirement; unreachable alone is insufficient.
Interrupted work used supported graceful Pod termination; no claim that SIGKILL releases native locks.
Synthetic repository data; no consumer application coordination or acceptance is included.

cleanup.namespaces: All owned qualification namespaces removed; only default and Kubernetes system namespaces remained before server deletion.
cleanup.billingNote: Observed hourly server and IPv4 prices rounded up to two whole hours for the entire shared lab, including preliminary runs. Traffic remained within included allowance. Estimate, not invoice.

artifacts: Raw outputs and generated credentials/manifests stayed outside Git under /tmp/bartl-restic-lifecycle-1793643294467. Only this selected qualification record is retained in Git.
